newsitem.title: ITALY: Arafat says peace agreements must be respected.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says peace agreements must be respected.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, speaking during a business forum in northern Italy, said on Friday that a 1993 peace agreement signed by Israel and the PLO must be respected.
"We are not asking for the moon, we are asking for what has been agreed upon and what has been signed to be implemented," Arafat said.
Arafat again emphasised that his landmark meeting with newly-elected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at a brief summit on Wednesday was important, above all because it happened.
"We hope that this will push the implementation of what has been agreed upon and what has been signed," he said.
Asked whether the Oslo accord on Palestinian self-rule could be rewritten, Arafat replied:
"Netanyahu has to remember it is not a bilateral agreement. It is an international agreement."
He said the agreement was supervised by the United States, Russia and Egypt and signed by the European Union.
"The documents have been recorded in the United Nations so that it is not a bilateral agreement. I haven't the right to change it, and he (Netanyahu) hasn't the right to change it."
The two sides are still apparently far apart on all major issues relating to continuation of the framework peace deal.

Palestinians want the implementation of peace deal clauses on an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron and other areas of the West Bank, and the opening of a passage for Palestinians to travel between the West Bank and Gaza.
Netanyahu argues that there can be no expansion of Palestinian self-rule unless Israel's security needs are satisfied.
Arafat also said that Iraq's action in moving troops and tanks into northern Kurdish areas of Iraq, prompting U.S. cruise missile strikes this week, was understandable.
"This is not a big story," he declared. "The Iraqis were obliged to move because the Iranians are supporting Jalal Talabani so they had to defend their international borders."
Iraq backs the Kurdish Democratic Party (KDP) against the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) led by Talabani.
